claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

informal_arrangement.description: Whether the claimant is looking after someone else's child through an informal arrangement.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 11 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with you in the UK.

Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's the thing - I look after Alex and he lives with me, but I'm not actually his parent. It's more of an informal arrangement where I've taken him in and I'm caring for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Informal arrangements are covered by Child Benefit rules, so that's helpful to know.

**Can you tell me a bit more about the arrangement? For example:**
- **Is Alex a friend or relative's child?**
- **Is your local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is a relative's child - I've just taken him in to help out the family. And no, the local council isn't paying me anything towards his costs or maintenance. I'm just doing this on my own to support him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. That's very helpful.

Just to confirm a few final details:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? For example, is one of his parents or another relative claiming it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
✓ You both live in the UK
✓ Alex lives with you and you're responsible for his care
✓ You have an informal arrangement to look after a relative's child, which is covered by Child Benefit rules
✓ The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You meet all the criteria for Child Benefit. You can proceed with making a claim for Alex. 

If you need help with the application process, you can contact the Child Benefit Office or make a claim through the official channels.

Additionally, no one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, which is important since only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. Based on all these factors, the claimant qualifies for Child Benefit for Alex.
